newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, Lebanon, Egypt cross-list shares Monday.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, Lebanon, Egypt cross-list shares Monday.

text.p: Kuwait, Lebanon and Egypt will cross-list shares on each other's exchanges from Monday, a representative of the three bourses said on Saturday.
"On Monday the agreement will take effect," General Secretary of the Union of Arab Stock Exchanges and Securities Commissions Sa'faq al-Rukeibi told Reuters.
Egypt and Kuwait signed an accord in April to cross-list shares. Lebanon joined in September.

"The main aim of the project is to ease procedures for investors. They can trade shares in the other exchanges through the same broker at their exchange," said Rukeibi, who is also head of the Kuwait Stock Exchange's technical department.

Rukeibi noted that the right to trade or own Kuwaiti shares remains exclusive to nationals of the Gulf Cooperation council (GCC) countries -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

Kuwaiti officials say they are considering opening the market for foreign investors, a move that requires the approval of the cabinet, parliament and the emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah. No timetable for the reform has been announced.
Egypt and Lebanon have no restrictions on foreigners trading shares of national firms.
However, Kuwait allows listing of shares of foreign companies subject to rules set by a market committee. Foreign residents can trade in mutual funds ran by local firms.

"The accord allows Arab residents in Kuwait to invest their money in Egyptian and Lebanese shares. It also allows GCC nationals living in Egupt or Lebanon to trade Kuwaiti shares at exchanges there. Cash abundance in Kuwait could boost trade at the Egyptian and Lebanese bourses," said Rukeibi.
The new investment channels are expected to result in a slight decline in trade of Kuwaiti shares, some dealers said.

"There will not be a big impact. Egyptian, Lebanese and other shares have always been availbale for Kuwaiti dealers. The only difference is that it will be easier to buy and sell those shares," said a portfolio manager.
Cross-listing "would encourage the establishment of joint financial firms in Arab states," said Rukeibi.
"In the light of the large groupings worldwide there must be similar Arab groupings to match them," he said.
Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman signed in December a similar accord to link their bourses.
